## Updates

`kaigen self-update --json` replaces the CLI with the latest release (`{"updated":true,"from":"…","to":"…"}`, or
`{"updated":false,…}` when current). Once a day `kaigen` prints one line on stderr when a newer release is out. A CLI
below the supported minimum answers every command with `update_required`: run `kaigen self-update`. This document
updates separately: if a command here does not match the binary, the binary wins (`kaigen --help`); the current copy

findings.remediation: Prevent the skill from modifying its own code, SKILL.md, or configuration files. Treat skill files as read-only at runtime.

## When Kaigen itself is broken: offer a report
findings.message: Skill modifies its own code, configuration, or behavior at runtime. Self-modification enables an agent to escalate privileges, disable safety constraints, or install persistent backdoors.
findings.remediation: Prevent the skill from modifying its own code, SKILL.md, or configuration files. Treat skill files as read-only at runtime.

findings.code_snippet:
macOS and Linux:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://api.kaigen3d.com/install.sh | sh   # installs ~/.kaigen/bin/kaigen and adds it to your shell profile
export PATH="$HOME/.kaigen/bin:$PATH"                 # this shell only: new shells already have it
kaigen login --json
kaigen doctor --json
findings.message: Remote code is downloaded and executed. This bypasses code review and could introduce malicious code.
findings.remediation: Avoid downloading and executing remote scripts. Use trusted packages from PyPI/npm. If remote fetch is required, verify checksums and use HTTPS.

findings.code_snippet:
installs the engine, makes games and publishes them to play.kaigen3d.com. It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux
(x86_64).

This skill covers **getting from nothing to a published game**. Once a game exists, the engine ships its own skills
under `<game>/.claude/skills` (and `.agents/skills`): read those for gameplay, rendering, shaders and builds.

## The whole path
findings.message: Skill enumerates or reads other installed skills. Access to other skills' SKILL.md files or the skills directory reveals prompt instructions, capabilities, and secrets that should be invisible to peer skills.
findings.remediation: Remove all code or instructions that list or read other skills' files or directories. Skills should operate independently; cross-skill access is a privilege escalation.

findings.code_snippet:
Windows (PowerShell):

```powershell
irm https://api.kaigen3d.com/install.ps1 | iex   # installs %LOCALAPPDATA%\kaigen\bin\kaigen.exe and puts it on PATH
kaigen login --json                              # the user approves in their browser (see "Sign in")
kaigen doctor --json                             # do what every failed check's remediation says
kaigen engine install
findings.message: Data is being sent to an external URL. This could be legitimate telemetry or data exfiltration. Manual review is recommended.
findings.remediation: Verify the destination URL is trusted and necessary. Remove or replace with documented APIs. Ensure no secrets, tokens, or PII are transmitted.

findings.code_snippet:
`kaigen version --json`.

`KAIGEN_HOME` relocates the CLI to `$KAIGEN_HOME/bin`. It must reach the `sh` on the right of the pipe:
`curl -fsSL https://api.kaigen3d.com/install.sh | KAIGEN_HOME=/opt/kaigen sh`. On Windows set it first:
`$env:KAIGEN_HOME = "D:\kaigen"; irm https://api.kaigen3d.com/install.ps1 | iex`.
